motion.name: completion

motion.name: blocked-beacon
motion.value: 6s directional light sweep and linear reflector rotation; light raster updates at 20fps
motion.purpose: Amber illumination on a fixed pixel grid behind manually blocked sites. Pauses offscreen and while the tab is hidden. Reduced motion uses a steady light pool and static reflector; motion never changes work state.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable CSS transitions and smooth scrolling; freeze sprite poses and omit particles.

breakpoints.purpose: Full-width canvas; floating crew and popup details rather than side columns.

breakpoints.name: compact-desktop

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Full-width canvas; floating crew and popup details rather than side columns.

masonry.columns: 12 initial; signed horizontal movement remains unbounded
masonry.columnWidth: 64px keyboard stride; 8px drag grid plus contact-edge snaps
masonry.verticalUnit: Exact body edges; no extra margin
masonry.diggerHeadroom: 48px open surface shaft; deeper shafts follow exposure, never padded body reservations
masonry.placement: Solid colored rectangles pack without overlap against body contact edges or dependency depth floors. Uncertainty adds no collision padding.
masonry.excavation: Completed colored bodies reserve their exact bounds; exposed top-face intervals open shafts to the surface. Shafts and cavities paint as one clipped dark union.
masonry.growth: Bounded viewport scrolls independently, with world depth derived from content and layout at a minimum of 1160px. Work and placement previews can extend depth; vertical scrolling, panning, and bottom-edge autoscrolling do not generate empty ground. Both horizontal directions remain unbounded. Terrain and discoveries are painted only near the viewport.

resize.behavior: Resize known scope independently of uncertainty. Repack around fixed excavations. Custom dimensions persist; presets reset them. Escape discards the preview.

dependencies.ports: 26px green circular input/output, 7px inside the top-right and bottom-right face corners, separate from resize grips
dependencies.lines: Orthogonal cream/green lines with dark under-strokes and compact 9px user-space arrowheads sharing the same stroke and colors. Selected and invalid states match their respective arrowheads.
dependencies.interaction: Drag from a prerequisite output onto dependent work; keyboard/click source then target also works. Multiple prerequisites; no self, duplicate, or cyclic links.
dependencies.ordering: Stable topological packing keeps every dependent below its prerequisites. Overhead body projections additionally determine which top-face intervals are accessible to diggers.

masonry.uncertaintyVisual: Alpha mask seeded at 28% across the full body beneath opaque 4px ordered Bayer pixels. Higher uncertainty enlarges the obscured vertical middle; soil texture shows through its faint block tint while the full estimated footprint stays discernible. Known material and the final bottom pixels remain opaque. 0% uses mask:none. Face, inset bevels, texture, and cracks share the mask and stepped corner clip. Readable labels and controls remain unmasked; outer speckles and collision padding are removed.
masonry.availability: Ready work keeps its chosen stone color, including unassigned ready work. Buried, prerequisite-waiting, and manually blocked work applies the same saturate(.74) brightness(.95) filter to the stone surface and number/title group, keeping ink and color backings consistent. Diggers, crew, presence, and barriers retain their colors; the uncertainty mask is unchanged. Number, title, and any progress percentage remain visible; accessible descriptions and details explain availability. Drag previews update the treatment from the preview layout. Completed cards retain their Cleared label.
masonry.fractures: Deterministic edge-rooted lightning trees. Progress extends connected jagged trunks inward and reveals smaller forks and secondary branches; 2px/1px weights remain fixed. Shared uncertainty mask.

keyboardNavigation.formFocus: New and edit block popups focus the title immediately; saving returns focus to the saved block and brings its world footprint into view.
keyboardNavigation.newBlock: Idle-canvas N creates below the last-created unfinished block, then the selected unfinished block, inheriting its color and width; otherwise it uses normal creation. Existing sign-in requirements apply.
keyboardNavigation.goToBlock: G opens the bottom-center Go to block form and focuses its numeric text field. Stable block numbers support multiple digits with a 650ms typing pause; Enter or Go submits immediately. Missing numbers show an inline status error and invalid field. Escape, Close, or outside click cancels.
keyboardNavigation.navigation: Select and focus the target, center its world footprint, and fit within 60–100% zoom. Completed work reveals its cavity card with browser-local visibility and stays completed. Smooth scrolling becomes immediate under reduced motion. Available to signed-out viewers.
keyboardNavigation.guards: Ignore typing, composition, held-key repeats, Command/Ctrl/Alt combinations, open dialogs, menus and forms, and active drag/pan gestures.

blockedSites.control: Labeled native checkbox with switch semantics before progress in unfinished block details; 38×24px pill track and 16px thumb, amber when checked. Uses existing focus and signed-out disabled behavior.
blockedSites.barrier: Centered 112×44px striped pixel construction barrier above the stone face, with square feet and a slowly rotating amber beacon. Decorative and pointer-transparent; phase captions avoid its bounds.
blockedSites.lighting: Fixed 144×108 raster scaled to 576×432 world pixels in 4px cells, screen-blended behind the stone face and details. Directional amber sweep with faint spill, bright yellow near the lamp and deeper ochre toward shadows. Exponential and edge falloff with stationary Bayer dithering fades into darkness without blur or pixel-grid rotation.
blockedSites.status: The block’s accessible description and details popup explain manual closure separately from prerequisite waiting and buried work. The barrier and beacon remain nontext cues; live block faces show no routine status badge.
blockedSites.behavior: Enabling clears every assignment atomically with the flag and prevents assignment and progress. Disabling removes the barrier and leaves assignments empty. Existing progress, dimensions, uncertainty, and dependencies remain intact. The flag saves, syncs, and participates in undo/redo.

diggerAppearance.hardhat: Hardhats have a narrower, taller crown, a projecting brim with a shaded underside, and one raised central rib with two side ribs. Highlights and shadows derive from the worker's chosen helmet color.
diggerAppearance.headphones: Headphones sit beneath the hardhat. The fitted band is concealed inside the helmet shell, while the ear cups remain visible below the brim. This layering preserves the crown, raised ribs, and brim across poses, facing directions, and glasses settings.
diggerAppearance.face: Faces use a symmetrical 16px-wide silhouette with paired ears and a centered chin. Both forward-facing eyes are 2×2px pupils on the same row, spaced 8px apart. Glasses use matching 6×6px frames with centered 4×4px inner lenses; pupils remain visible above the lens fill. The face and glasses stay aligned through bobbing poses, mirrored facing, hair, headphones, and the existing hardhat.

diggerAnimation.clock: Independent seeded clock per person/site, preserved across rerenders; phase and 155–235ms pickaxe tempo vary.
diggerAnimation.breaks: Coffee and phone pauses last 2.8–5.4 seconds between longer digging stretches.
diggerAnimation.walking: Short walks in personal lanes within an exposed ledge; 8px worker spacing. No crossing buried ground. Frozen during block, resize, and person drags.
diggerAnimation.progress: Ambient only; no task or save mutations. Reduced motion is stationary.

workspace.layout: One canvas filling available width and height; no permanent sidebars or separate project action strip. 52px header, 44px toolbar, compact 30px legend; 12px gutters. Below 680px: 44px header, 76px two-row toolbar, 6px gutters; all controls remain available.
workspace.crew: 236px floating tray, initially at top left, with sprite, name, and placement LEDs; collapses to 104px. Mobile starts collapsed. Existing drag and click assignment interactions remain. The Crew header has a move icon, grab/grabbing cursors, and a focusable Move crew palette button using the existing green focus color. Dragging moves the tray in screen space within the canvas with an 8px edge inset, independently of terrain pan and zoom. Arrow keys move 8px, Shift moves 32px, Home resets, and Escape cancels an active drag. Browser-local normalized position survives reload, viewport resizing, and expand/collapse without project sync or undo history. Manage crew and collapse retain their actions. Phase captions recalculate their obstacle around the moved tray.
workspace.inspector: Native nonmodal popover on block/cavity click, 344px wide with natural content height capped at min(660px, viewport height minus 24px) and 12px viewport clamp. Fixed chrome keeps Close available above an independently scrolling body. The shared styles.css #inspector rule uses flex: 1 1 auto and min-height: 0; preserve its content basis to prevent Safari auto-height collapse. Progress/unknown/assignments first; Size & prerequisites expandable. Compact notes and assignment chips.
workspace.dismissal: Escape, Close, outside click, or canvas wheel/pan. Keyboard activation supported and focus returns to the source on explicit close. Save/create returns to canvas.
workspace.completed: Cleared menu in the toolbar and existing cavity markers. Reset is in Help.
workspace.toolbar: Project name, demo badge, crew presence, Cleared, and Phases share the toolbar. Add block sits immediately after Undo/Redo and before zoom/reset. Mobile puts project name, Cleared, and Phases above the complete action row.
workspace.projectDetails: Header/toolbar project-name buttons and the surface sign open the native Edit project modal. Required project name and optional sign subtitle, each up to 80 characters. Explicit Save changes trims and commits both as one undoable shared edit. Cancel/Close/Escape discard; focus changes do not save. Remote updates defer while the draft is open. Paper dialog at most 420px wide with viewport-clamped scrolling and 16px mobile fields.
workspace.terrainProps: Decorative fixed-world pixel scenery follows terrain pan and zoom without project state or interactions. Blue porta-potty remains on the main terrain at x=840, y=12, base y=88, beside the surface fence; pale roof, inset vented door, latch, and green vacant indicator. A separate viewport-windowed discovery canvas paints scattered dinosaur remains at x=328, top y=576 (60 8px units below the surface): skull, separated short tail, two ribs, and one thigh in muted bone tones at 0.45 opacity. A helmeted dwarf at x=768, top y=1536 (180 units) has a full copper beard, dark sideburns, two alternating braided locks with gold clasps and tapered ends, a curled moustache, raised brow, rosy cheeks, and a crooked toothy grin. Leather suspenders and wide planted boots anchor six 180ms pickaxe poses: ready, windup, lift, strike, follow-through, and recovery, with shoulder lean, bobbing, a two-handed grip, and impact sparks. A shadowy winged, horned balrog at x=464, top y=2016 (240 units) stands 24px into a stepped rock arch with a soot-dark chamber, warm faceted stones, rubble, and an ember-strewn floor. Eight idle poses over 2880ms combine breathing and expanding shoulders, weight shifts on planted boots and bent legs, wing flex and droop, head turns and eyelids, and arm and whip sway. Fire, coals, and rising embers use separate 180ms stepped flicker. Cave and all poses fit the 248px discovery height used for viewport culling. Full live-block footprints, including uncertain regions, and all cavities and shafts are cleared from discoveries. The existing animation loop refreshes discoveries at about 140ms intervals; reduced motion is static, and hidden pages pause.
workspace.surfaceSign: Timber sign at world x=280; DOM text at x=294 shares the exported scene origin. Clear of expanded desktop and default collapsed mobile crew. Shovel at x=580. Project name always present in Pixel type; optional DM subtitle below. Blank omits subtitle; long lines ellipsize with full-text tooltip. Keyboard-accessible edit button.
workspace.zoom: Command/Ctrl plus scroll over the excavation zooms 60–135% around the cursor. Ordinary scrolling is unchanged. Nonpassive prevention owns modified scrolling even at limits; active drag/pan gestures and the project modal guard changes. Local view state only.

remoteSelections.appearance: Active remote selections retain matching colored rings. Each of up to four distinct people has a 28px circle in their presence color, with a 2px cream border and white semibold 10px initials. A matching 20×24px SVG cursor arrow above-left points into the block, with a 2px cream stroke.
remoteSelections.layout: The first circle is centered on the block’s bottom-right corner, half overhanging both edges. Additional circles extend side by side to the left at 34px intervals. Inverse scaling below 100% terrain zoom preserves the markers’ on-screen size.
remoteSelections.accessibility: The selection’s accessible label retains every selecting person’s full name. Visual markers are aria-hidden and the overlay uses pointer-events: none.

placementSlots.appearance: One crisp 6×6px stepped, recessed pixel LED per available placement in crew palette buttons and the active Manage crew roster. Unused slots are dim; assigned slots are active green. Hard pixel edges remain distinct in both states.
placementSlots.layout: Up to four columns and two rows for one to eight slots. Exact assignment counts remain in accessible labels and tooltips.
placementSlots.control: Manage crew uses a labeled native Placements per digger number field with visible up/down steppers and an explicit Save limit action, using existing field and button styles. The field is required and accepts integers from one to eight with step one. Clearing it preserves a blank editing draft; a successful save normalizes the displayed number. Width is 88px with a 40px desktop minimum height; below 680px, the field and Save limit action have a 44px minimum height, and the field font is 16px. The project defaults to two placements per digger, including older projects. The active roster scrolls within the dialog to keep controls and the footer reachable on short mobile screens.

brandMark.appearance: Centered pixel shovel with a compact solid copper T-grip, timber shaft, brass collar, and shaded teal steel blade with symmetric sides that remain full-width to y=28 before tapering through unequal orthogonal pixel steps to a softened four-pixel-wide tip across the bottom two rows, rivets, and a central ridge. The narrower, taller blade spans 16×18 units (x=8–24, y=18–36) within the 32×36px grid. The horizontal T-bar is 12px wide and 4px high, 75% of the blade’s width. Silhouette, shading, and ridge use only horizontal and vertical path segments.
brandMark.usage: Static decorative header image beside the Silkscreen wordmark, also used as the favicon. Preserve the green period and cream-paper setting.
brandMark.responsive: 32×36px on desktop; 28×32px below 680px; hidden at 360px and below.

narrative.overview:
A pixel-art excavation sits inside a quiet cream-paper workbench. Earth and stone textures, colored work blocks, and small diggers make the project tangible; restrained sans-serif controls keep the scene usable.

This documents the implemented prototype and the user’s confirmed digging direction. Depth communicates sequence, soft pixel edges communicate uncertain scope, and cracks communicate manually reported progress. Pickaxe movement communicates activity only.
keyCharacteristics: Cream-paper controls around a dark, textured excavation.
Pixel typography for scene labels; DM Sans for readable controls and task names.
Ten work block colors with paired stone shades, chosen from two rows of five swatches; adjustable uncertainty and several visible diggers.
Manual progress, with no date or time axis.
dos: Do keep the excavation central and controls on light paper surfaces.
Do render terrain, cracks, dithering, and sprites with crisp pixel edges.
Do distinguish the known beginning and end from the dithered unknown middle.
Do preserve text and focus cues alongside color and animation.
Do keep progress deliberate and the mobile scene pannable.
donts: Don’t turn excavation depth or block dimensions into deadlines or duration.
Don’t advance progress from pickaxe animation.
Don’t replace readable interface text with pixel typography throughout.
Don’t let decorative terrain compete with the colored work blocks.
